findings.finding: The release carries the first FY27 guide, and the issuer (CFO, now interim CEO) has already told the market FY27 includes a rebuild of the cost base (variable pay) and only 'progress towards' medium-term targets (revenue HSD, EBITDA margin in the 60s), which tilts the first EBITDA guide toward disappointing a sell-side that has HBX on a recovery path; this name fell 12.0% on its last first-guide day (26 Nov 2025) and 27.4% on a guide trim (30 Jul 2025).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide events: 30 Jul 2025 guide trim -27.4%; 26 Nov 2025 FY25 results with first FY26 guide -12.0%; 13 May 2026 guide cut (pre-flagged, stock already low) -1.0%; 29 Jul 2026 narrowing -0.7% then +3.6% next session (Yahoo daily closes HBX.MC).
findings.why_not_priced: The cost-rebuild remark is public but qualitative; there is no FY27 consensus visible (the company's own consensus page is FY26-only, compiled in August) and the shares trade at ~EUR7.95 against average targets above EUR11, i.e. the sell-side still models recovery. If the cost rebuild were priced, the stock would have de-rated into the print; instead it has been flat (20d +0.95%, 60d +6.8%).
findings.independence: Interim CEO is the former CFO who owns the guide, which argues against a kitchen-sink reset (cuts the size); WebBeds' upgraded 1H27 and Expedia B2B strength (finding 2) point the other way for the TTV/revenue legs of the guide. none pointing the same way.

findings.finding: Counterparties/peers that reported after HBX's July update show strong B2B hotel demand in HBX's Q4 (Jul-Sep) and into FY27: Expedia Q3 B2B gross bookings +19% with double-digit growth in every region, and WebBeds (closest listed bedbank peer) upgraded 1H27 (Apr-Sep) EUR revenue to +14-16% from +11-15% with TTV margin rising to at least 6.7% and Europe/MEA/APAC improving in its second quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: HBX's TTV has beaten the market repeatedly (9M +15% cc) yet revenue/take rate disappointed; the stock has traded on revenue and EBITDA, not TTV, on every print since IPO.
findings.why_not_priced: Peer read-across is a proxy and partly priced (HBX +2-3% around 2-4 Nov). Q4 FY26 lands inside a narrowed guide, so it mostly matters for the FY27 TTV/revenue starting point; a priced version would show HBX re-rating with WebBeds after its August upgrade, which it did not do materially. Note WebBeds' margin expansion contrasts with HBX's take-rate compression, so the read-across to HBX revenue is weaker than to TTV.
findings.independence: WebBeds 1H27 guidance upgrade, https://webbedsgroup.com/news/2026-agm/ (AGM, late Aug 2026), a different company and document from Expedia.

findings.finding: Capital return: the EUR100m buyback runs to 30 Sep 2027 with c.EUR50m returned in FY26 by July and leverage at 1.5-1.7x inside a 1-2x range management called comfortable; a final dividend under the 20% payout policy is due with the release.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Buyback/dividend announcement 16 Jan 2026: stock rose on the start of the programme (+4% reported by Estrategias de Inversion, 13 Feb 2026).
findings.why_not_priced: Policy is known, so only an extension or top-up would be new; small by construction.
